# SOP-P3-L1-01 Line startup - Hot Forge line
Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P3, line P3-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, EQ-P3-L1-IH03  
Related documents: SB-1044, SOP-P3-L1-02, SOP-P3-L1-04

Purpose
This standard operating procedure (SOP) defines the required preconditions, personal protective equipment (PPE), step-by-step startup actions, verification checks, rationale, examples of common anomalies and required records for bringing the Hot Forge line up to production-ready status. This procedure applies to operators and maintenance personnel responsible for EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03.

Preconditions
1. Maintenance clearance and lockout/tagout completed per SOP-P3-L1-02.  
2. Preventive maintenance for EQ-P3-L1-SB02 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01 completed and documented in SB-1044.  
3. Tooling, material, and loading fixtures staged at the work point.  
4. Required consumables and lubricant on-site: The lubricant part number for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is CFW-LUB-278.  
5. Control system in local mode and interlocks confirmed functional per SOP-P3-L1-04.

PPE
- Protective gloves rated for heat handling and abrasion.  
- Safety glasses with side protection.  
- Face shield for operations at the blast cabinet.  
- Hearing protection per plant requirements.  
- Flame-resistant clothing when handling heated charge material.  

Startup Steps (numbered sequence)
1. Visual walkdown and area clearance  
   1.1. Confirm no tools, debris, or nonessential personnel are in the line path.  
   1.2. Verify guards and access doors are closed and latched on EQ-P3-L1-HP01, EQ-P3-L1-SB02, and EQ-P3-L1-IH03. Rationale: guards prevent exposure to moving components and thermal hazards.

2. Utilities and systems check  
   2.1. Confirm air, power, and operational pneumatic/hydraulic supply indicators are present and within normal operating indications on local panels. Rationale: ensures actuators and controls will respond during startup. Example: if a supply gauge shows no pressure indicator, suspend startup and call maintenance per SOP-P3-L1-02.

3. Control system initialization  
   3.1. Place PLC/operator station in startup mode and perform the software boot sequence per manufacturer prompts. Rationale: proper initialization avoids false alarms and ensures correct interlock behavior.  
   3.2. Verify alarm log is clear of critical faults before enabling actuators.

4. Shot blast cabinet specific verification (EQ-P3-L1-SB02)  
   4.1. Confirm blast media bin is adequately filled and the media delivery path is unobstructed.  
   4.2. Inspect blast wheel liner and fasteners. If any fastener is suspected loose, torque to the required value: The blast wheel liner bolt torque for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #2 (EQ-P3-L1-SB02) is 65 N·m. Rationale: correct torque prevents liner displacement and wheel imbalance. Example: a slightly loose liner bolt can manifest as increased vibration; torque to specified value and recheck vibration after brief operation.

5. Heater and induction systems (EQ-P3-L1-IH03 and EQ-P3-L1-HP01) checks  
   5.1. Verify heat source power enable interlocks and sensors report nominal status on the operator panel. Rationale: prevents applying heat without flow or cooling where required.  
   5.2. Confirm any cooling or quench circuits are active and free of leaks.

6. Dry run with no load  
   6.1. With PPE donned, run the line through its startup sequence without material loaded. Observe for unusual noise, vibration, smoke, or smells. Rationale: isolated verification reduces risk to product and personnel. Example: if a conveyor mis-tracks during dry run, stop and realign before loading.

7. Functional checks with sample load  
   7.1. Introduce a controlled sample part and run through the full process route. Verify part handling, indexing accuracy, and process cycle continuity. Rationale: confirms integration of subsystems under real load conditions.  
   7.2. Monitor quality indicators at process checkpoints; if defects are observed, halt production and follow troubleshooting per SOP-P3-L1-04.

8. Final go/no-go verification  
   8.1. Confirm all critical alarms are clear and historical errors resolved.  
   8.2. Notify line lead and production control that line is ready for production start.

Records to keep
- Startup checklist completed and signed. Include operator initials and timestamps.  
- Torque verification record for blast wheel liner bolts on EQ-P3-L1-SB02 recording the applied value: 65 N·m and the lubricant used: CFW-LUB-278. Store this record with PM documentation referenced in SB-1044.  
- Dry run and sample run observation log including anomalies and corrective actions.  
- Any maintenance work orders raised during startup referenced to SOP-P3-L1-02.

Step rationale and examples
- Torque specification example: Correctly torqued blast wheel liner bolts reduce the likelihood of liner failure and imbalanced operation which can cause downstream galling or bearing damage. Recording the applied torque and lubricant ensures traceability for future failure analysis.  
- Dry run rationale example: Running equipment unloaded allows detection of misalignment and loose components without risking parts or process contamination. Common anomalies include loose fasteners, belt tracking issues, and sensor misreads; each should be documented and remediated prior to production.

Abnormal conditions and escalation
- If any critical interlock fails to reset, stop the startup sequence and engage maintenance following SOP-P3-L1-02.  
- If vibration or thermal anomalies persist after corrective action, tag the equipment out and notify engineering per SOP-P3-L1-04.

Sign-off
- Operator name and signature: _______________________  
- Shift supervisor name and signature: _______________________  
- Maintenance verifier name and signature: _______________________  

Retain completed SOP and attached records according to plant document control policy and file with SB-1044 documentation.
